c.tagline: Okinawa's laid-back capital, where Ryukyu castles, island cuisine, and East China Sea beaches replace mainland Japan's rush.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are plentiful, cheap, and metered - usually the practical choice, since ride-hailing apps barely operate in Okinawa. GO and DiDi have only limited taxi-dispatch coverage in Naha; otherwise flag one on the street or wait at a rank.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police and 119 reaches fire and ambulance, nationwide.

avoid.reason: Ignore bar touts on Kokusai-dori and in the Matsuyama nightlife district late at night to avoid inflated-bill scams.

hood_desc: The mile-long 'International Street' and the covered Makishi Public Market form the city's lively heart - souvenir shops, izakayas, Okinawan restaurants, and hotels; the obvious walkable base for first-timers.
The former royal capital on the hills east of downtown, centered on the reconstructed Shuri Castle, stone-paved lanes, and sacred Ryukyu sites; quieter and steeped in history.
A modern 'new downtown' of shopping malls, the Okinawa Prefectural Museum, duty-free shops, and upscale hotels built on former US military land; polished and easy to reach by monorail.
The seaside pocket around Naminoue Shrine and Naha's only city beach, plus the old Wakasa port district; relaxed and close to the center.
Naha's historic pottery quarter of narrow lanes, working kilns, ceramic studios, and cafes just off the Makishi market; arty and atmospheric.
lodging: Hotel Aqua Citta Naha by WBF

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though some prefer bottled for taste.

transit.pay: Tap a contactless IC card (national Suica/ICOCA or the local OKICA) or buy a paper ticket at Yui Rail stations; a single monorail ride is about ¥230-370 by distance, and the 1-day and 2-day passes are good value. Buses take cash, OKICA, and now most national IC cards.
transit.hours: The Yui Rail monorail runs roughly 6 AM to midnight; city buses run daytime into the evening with sparser night service, so taxis fill late-night trips.
transit.note: The Yui Rail monorail is the prefecture's only train - a single elevated line running from Naha Airport through Kokusai-dori and Omoromachi up to Shuri and Tedako-Uranishi. Buses cover everywhere else, but to explore the wider island most visitors rent a car.

ferry: Ferries to the Kerama Islands and Kagoshima

transit.m: Yui Rail monorail to Kokusai-dori (Kenchō-mae), ~12 min
Yui Rail monorail to Shuri, ~27 min

tip.r: Not customary; no tipping is expected anywhere, and leaving money can cause confusion.
